In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of cultural identity in three Afro-American novels,probing into the identity pursuit of the black in American society.
the issue of identity pursuit in Afro-American literature, and we have made a brief analysis on Richard Wright's Native Son, Ralph Ellison's Invisible Man, Toni Morrison's Beloved.
the following questions: How do black writers explore the cultural identity of black in their works?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three writers have different views of the pursuit of identity in Afro-American literature.
the identity pursuit in the three writers is a long and tortuous process, which can be achieved by the black only when they find their roots and traditional culture.
the black identity pursuit is the pursuit to find their own roots.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identity pursuit is the symbol of the black's spiritual rebirth and the pursuit of authentic existence.
the identity pursuit in Afro-American literature can be divided into three stages: protest,dormancy,and flight.
the three writers are in the same pursuit of the cultural identity of the Afro-American people,while their works reflect different aspects of the cultural identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the black people should find their cultural identity and root in order to get a sense of self.
the black writers in the 20th century have a strong sense of identity, and they have made a significant contribution to the development of American literature.
we can find the identity pursuit of the Afro-American in the literature of different generations,which is an important part of their literature and culture.
